Requirements: Admission into the MSAT program is competitive. Applicants will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for all undergraduate coursework. Successful completion of prerequisite courses (listed on the program website) with a minimum grade of "C" (2.0 on a 4.0 scale). Minimum of 50 observation hours under the direct supervision of a Board of Certification (BOC) certified athletic trainer (ATC). Hours must be completed prior to the application deadline. Two letters of recommendation, one must be from a BOC certified athletic trainer (ATC). Letters must be submitted on the online application by the recommender. Completed Statement of Purpose (SOP) addressing: What are your professional goals? Why are you interested in becoming an athletic trainer? Why are you interested in pursuing the MSAT program at Kent State University? Why do you believe you would be a strong candidate for the MSAT program at Kent State University? Resume/CV. Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. Transcripts must be submitted directly from the institution to Kent State University. International applicants only: Proof of English Language Proficiency, e.g., TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo English Test. All applicants are required to interview with the MSAT admissions committee following review of their application materials. The GRE is NOT required for admission to the MSAT program.
Program name: Master of Science in Athletic Training

Requirements: Applicants to the Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants may apply prior to completion of a bachelor's degree, but must have earned the degree prior to beginning the graduate program. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Minimum 3.00 GPA on a 4.00 point scale for undergraduate coursework. Three letters of recommendation. A current resume (CV). A letter of intent/personal statement. Applicants must apply through the Communication Sciences and Disorders Centralized Application Service (CSDCAS) and the Kent State University Admissions Office. Applicants for the Au.D. program are encouraged to submit scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test, but GRE scores are not required for admission. All applicants must complete an interview with a member of the Au.D. Admissions Committee. Minimum English Language Proficiency Requirements (for international students only).
Program name: Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.)

Requirements: Admission to the Master of Arts degree program in Audiology is competitive. The following documents must be submitted to the Office of Graduate Admissions to be considered for admission: Official graduate application, official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000 point scale for regular admission, official GRE scores, a two-page statement of purpose that outlines the applicant's research interests, professional and academic goals, three letters of recommendation, and a baccalaureate degree in speech pathology and audiology or a related field. Minimum 12 credits in speech pathology and audiology courses, including one course in phonetics, one course in anatomy and physiology of the speech and hearing mechanism, one course in speech and hearing science, and one course in audiology or aural rehabilitation. Additional course requirements include statistics, biological sciences, physical sciences and social sciences.
Program name: Master of Arts in Audiology

Requirements: Applicants must meet the requirements for admission to the College of Graduate Studies, including a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in speech pathology and audiology or a related field. Minimum 3.000 GPA on a 4.000 point scale for undergraduate coursework. All applicants must submit official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a curriculum vitae/resume, a statement of purpose, a writing sample and GRE General Test scores. An interview is also required.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Audiology

Requirements: Official transcript(s); Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA; Goal statement; Letters of recommendation.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Autism Spectrum Disorders

Requirements: Applicants must meet the following requirements to be considered for admission: Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university, Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall, Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA in upper-division accounting courses (30000 level and above), Current professional resume, Statement of purpose, Two letters of recommendation, Official transcripts. International applicants must also meet English language proficiency requirements as defined in the university policy regarding international admissions. GRE/GMAT scores are not required for admission.
Program name: Master of Science in Accounting (M.S.A.)

Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Accounting Analytics program is selective. All applicants must meet the university graduate admission requirements as well as the program-specific requirements. A minimum 2.750 undergraduate cumulative GPA on a 4.000-point scale. Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework. Goal statement describing the applicant's purpose in undertaking graduate study in accounting analytics. Three letters of recommendation. Resume. For applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 550 PBT (paper-based test), 79 iBT (internet-based test) or 6.5 on the IELTS.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Accounting Analytics
Graduate Certificate in Accounting Fundamentals

Requirements: Admission to the M.S. in Accounting, Business Technology and Analytics is open to applicants who hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Strong applicants should demonstrate academic excellence through prior coursework in accounting and related business fields. Applicants with insufficient prior coursework in accounting and/or business will be required to complete foundational coursework. Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA overall or in the last two years of undergraduate coursework. All applicants are required to take the GMAT or GRE. Applicants with strong academic credentials may request a waiver for the GMAT/GRE. Please contact the Department of Accounting for information on the waiver policy.
Program name: Master of Science in Accounting, Business Technology and Analytics

Requirements:
Admission Requirements
Application materials for admission to the M.F.A. in Acting program are submitted through the university’s online application system. The program accepts applications in the fall for admission the following fall. The application deadline is December 15.

Required application materials include:
*   Online application
*   Application fee
*   Official transcripts
*   Statement of purpose (should be 1-2 pages in length and include your reasons for pursuing graduate work, your specific area of interest within the field, and your professional goals.)
*   Resume/CV
*   Three (3) letters of recommendation

All applicants must undergo an audition/interview to be considered for admission to the program. Audition/interview dates for admission in Fall 2024 (and subsequent years) are as follows:
*   Saturday, January 20, 2024 at Kent State University (by invitation only)
*   Friday, February 9, 2024 at University Resident Theatre Association (URTA) Unified Auditions in Chicago (for URTA members only)
All URTA and On-Campus Auditions will be scheduled after a completed application has been submitted and reviewed.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Acting

Requirements:
The post-bachelor’s Graduate Certificate in Addictions Counseling requires candidates to have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the admission criteria for the School of Lifespan Development and Educational Sciences.

Application Materials:

Statement of purpose/letter of interest (one-to-two pages)
Official transcripts (all undergraduate and graduate work)
3 letters of recommendation
Official GRE scores (GRE is not required)
Resume/CV (optional)
Application for Graduate Admission
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Addictions Counseling

Requirements: Applicants must meet the requirements for admission to the College of Nursing. Official transcript(s), a minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA on a 4.000 point scale in the master’s degree, Master’s degree in Nursing from an accredited institution, current, unrestricted R.N. license in the United States, including current active Registered Nurse license in the state where practice will occur during the clinical experience, proof of national certification in an advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) specialty (e.g., Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS), Nurse Practitioner (NP), Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA) or Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM)), current CPR for healthcare providers, a personal statement that includes the following: Reasons for seeking certification, Area of specialization/population focus being sought, Experience to date related to the specialty, Future goals, Professional accomplishments, Resume or curriculum vitae, three professional letters of recommendation submitted directly from the evaluator, for international applicants, a TOEFL or IELTS score for whom English is not their native language, satisfy the College of Nursing graduate technology requirements. Interviews are conducted at the discretion of the College of Nursing.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner

Requirements: Baccalaureate in Nursing (BSN) from an ACEN or CCNE accredited program. Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000 point scale. An unencumbered RN license in at least one state. One year (2,000 hours) of full-time work experience as a registered nurse prior to application is preferred, not required. Successful completion of a college-level statistics course within the last five years with a grade of C or better. Resume (listing education and work experience). Statement of goals, including area of clinical interest and a description of previous experience. Two letters of recommendation (academic and/or professional). Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Application (complete the online application with payment of non-refundable application fee). International applicants have additional admission requirements.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult Gerontology Clinical Nurse Specialist

Requirements: Admission to the post-master’s certificate in Adult Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner requires applicants to meet the following criteria: Master's degree with a major in nursing from an accredited college or university, minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA, official transcripts, current, unencumbered RN license from the state in which clinical experiences will occur, three letters of recommendation, goal statement, Curriculum Vitae (CV), personal interview with the program coordinator. International students must meet Kent State University requirements for admission to graduate study.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner

Requirements: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended; Minimum 3.0 overall undergraduate GPA; Current, unencumbered RN license from any state in the United States. Must be valid at the time of application; Completion of an undergraduate statistics course with a minimum C grade, or its equivalent. Statistics must be completed prior to beginning coursework; Baccalaureate of Science in Nursing (B.S.N.) degree from an accredited program (ACEN, CCNE or CNEA); A personal interview with a faculty member. Applicants will be contacted to schedule an interview upon successful submission and review of all application materials.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Adult/Adolescent Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner

Requirements:
Application Requirements for the Graduate Certificate in Advanced Accounting include:
*   Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
*   Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000 point scale (for unconditional admission).
*   Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities.
*   Resume
*   Statement of purpose
*   GMAT/GRE is waived for students with a 3.000 undergraduate GPA or higher.
*   International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency.
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Advanced Accounting

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering program is granted to applicants who hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a closely related field. Students with other engineering or scientific backgrounds will be considered on a case-by-case basis and may be required to complete specific undergraduate coursework before being fully admitted to the program.

All applicants must have a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and 3.000 in major coursework for regular admission. Applicants with an overall undergraduate GPA between 2.200 and 2.749 or a major GPA below 3.000 may be considered for conditional admission.

Applicants for admission to the M.S. in Aerospace Engineering program must submit the following:
* Official transcripts (undergraduate and graduate, if applicable)
* Two letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of the applicant's academic and/or professional capabilities
* Statement of purpose describing the applicant's academic background and research interests, and their desire to pursue graduate study in aerospace engineering.
* Resume or curriculum vitae (CV)
* Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative, and analytical writing) are optional. International applicants must also submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Program name: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering

Requirements:
Applicants for the Ph.D. degree in Aerospace Engineering must meet the requirements of the College of Aeronautics and Engineering and the requirements of the Kent State University Graduate School as well as the following specific requirements:
A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering or a closely related field from an accredited institution.
A minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA on a 4.000 point scale for undergraduate and graduate coursework.
Official transcript(s).
GRE general test scores.
A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume.
A statement of purpose.
Three letters of recommendation.
For international applicants, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), 213 (computer-based) or 550 (paper-based), or a minimum IELTS score of 6.5.
Admission to the program is competitive, and meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Aerospace Engineering

Requirements: Admission to the Master of Arts degree program in Anthropology is competitive. Criteria for admission include: Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA (on a 4.000 point scale) overall and in the major. Official transcript(s). Statement of purpose addressing interest in the program and intended research area. Curriculum vitae or resume. Three letters of recommendation. Writing sample (typically a research paper or term paper from an undergraduate course). English language proficiency — international applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency (unless waived). GRE scores are not required.
Program name: Master of Arts in Anthropology

Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program in Applied Geology is competitive. Applicants typically have a master’s degree in geology or a closely related field from an accredited college or university, with a minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA. Exceptional applicants with a bachelor’s degree may be considered for direct admission. Official transcript(s), GRE General Test scores, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of purpose, Curriculum vitae (CV). International applicants must meet the English Language Proficiency policy and provide proof of English proficiency.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Geology

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the Kent State University Graduate School and those of the Department of Mathematical Sciences. To be considered for admission to the Applied Mathematics M.A. program, applicants must have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution and an undergraduate record demonstrating high academic achievement. Specific requirements for admission to the Applied Mathematics M.A. program are: A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall or in the last two years of undergraduate study. A minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA in mathematics. Baccalaureate courses in mathematics including Calculus I, II, III, Linear Algebra, Differential Equations and Introduction to Analysis (or Advanced Calculus). Additionally, students applying to our graduate programs must complete the online application through the Kent State University Office of Graduate Admissions. In addition to the online application form, the following items are required: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. A statement of purpose. Three (3) letters of recommendation from faculty members who are familiar with the applicant's academic work and potential for graduate study. A resume/curriculum vitae. International applicants whose native language is not English must provide proof of English language proficiency.
Program name: Master of Arts in Applied Mathematics

Requirements:
Applicants to the Master of Science in Applied Mathematics program must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. In addition, the following minimum requirements must be met:
* Minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA on a 4.000 point scale for undergraduate coursework.
* Official transcripts.
* A curriculum vitae or résumé.
* Three letters of recommendation.
* A statement of purpose.
* For applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), 213 (computer-based) or 550 (paper-based); or a minimum IELTS score of 6.5; or a minimum PTE Academic score of 58; or a minimum Duolingo score of 105.
* GRE general test is not required for admission.
Program name: Master of Science in Applied Mathematics

Requirements: Applicants to the Master of Architecture program must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. All applicants are evaluated individually by the graduate committee based on the following: A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall, Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, Statement of purpose, Resume/curriculum vitae (CV), Portfolio, GRE general test scores for applicants with an undergraduate GPA below 3.000 or for applicants from non-accredited institutions (For these applicants, the department recommends a minimum score of 153 on the verbal and 153 on the quantitative sections). For applicants whose first language is not English, the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) is required. The minimum acceptable score for admission is 550 PBT (paper-based test), or 79 IBT (internet-based test). In some cases, the graduate committee may recommend additional English language training for students with TOEFL scores between 550 and 600 PBT, or 79 and 99 IBT.
Program name: Master of Architecture

Requirements:
Applications are submitted through the College of Architecture and Environmental Design.
Required Documents:
*   Official Transcripts
*   Statement of Purpose (1-2 pages) describing the applicant’s academic and professional goals, experience, and interests relating to the MS.AED program at Kent State University.
*   Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV)
*   Three (3) Letters of Recommendation (professional or academic)
*   Portfolio (recommended, but not required). For applicants from other disciplines, a portfolio of relevant work that demonstrates visual or technical skills (e.g., drawings, photography, writing samples, coding, etc.).
*   International applicants must also provide English language proficiency exam scores if required by the Kent State University Office of Global Education. Visit the Global Education website for specific information regarding language requirements.
*   The GRE (Graduate Record Examination) is NOT required for admission to the MS.AED program.
Program name: Master of Science in Architecture and Environmental Design

Requirements: Applicants must satisfy the following additional requirements: A current resume or curriculum vitae outlining education, art teaching experience, other professional experience, exhibitions, and achievements. A letter of intent (statement of purpose) describing why the applicant is interested in the program and career goals. A portfolio of 10-15 images of artwork. Images should be in a JPEG format; no larger than 1920 pixels on the longest side and 72 dpi. Three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable about the applicant's academic and/or professional abilities. A professional writing sample (e.g., an excerpt from an academic paper, research report, or professional publication). Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Students must submit the online application form and pay the non-refundable application fee. International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. International applicants must submit an international credential evaluation by World Education Services (WES) or Educational Credential Evaluators (ECE).
Program name: Master of Arts in Art Education

Requirements: Admission to the M.A. program in Art History requires an undergraduate degree in Art History or a related field with at least a 3.000 cumulative GPA in undergraduate work. Other requirements for admission are as follows: The application for admission is submitted through the Office of Graduate Studies online application. A statement of purpose (approximately 500 words) describing the applicant’s academic background, interest in the M.A. program in Art History, and professional goals. A research paper or critical essay (8-10 pages) from an art history course or a related field that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to conduct research and write an analytical essay. Two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic work. A curriculum vitae detailing the applicant’s academic training and professional experience related to art history, including previous degrees, academic awards, publications, and exhibitions. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Applicants are not required to submit GRE scores for admission to the Art History M.A. program.
Program name: Master of Arts in Art History

Requirements: Applicants for admission to the Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence degree program must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in computer science, computer information systems, computer engineering, management information systems, data science or a closely related field. International applicants must meet the English language proficiency requirements. Students who do not have a bachelor’s degree in a closely related field may be admitted provisionally to the program. The provisional admission requires the student to complete a series of bridge courses to achieve the required background knowledge and skills. These bridge courses do not count toward the Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence degree. All applicants must meet the university requirements for graduate admission. In addition, applicants for the M.S. in Artificial Intelligence program must submit: Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, A statement of purpose (1-2 pages), A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV), Official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test scores, For international applicants, official TOEFL, IELTS, PTE or Duolingo English Test scores.
Program name: Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence

Requirements: Admission to the Master of Science in Aviation Management and Logistics program requires the following: Baccalaureate degree in a related field from an accredited college or university. Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA (on a 4.000 point scale) for unconditional admission. Conditional admission may be granted to applicants with a GPA between 2.200 and 2.749. International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency. Submit all application materials to the Office of Graduate Admissions. International students with undergraduate degrees from foreign universities should complete all prerequisite coursework prior to applying to the program.
Program name: Master of Science in Aviation Management and Logistics

Requirements:
Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements for admission into the Behavioral Intervention Specialist graduate certificate program:
*   Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA
*   One official transcript of undergraduate degree from an accredited institution
*   Resume
*   Two letters of recommendation
*   Statement of purpose (one to two pages, double-spaced)
*   Interview with the program coordinator
Program name: Graduate Certificate in Behavioral Intervention Specialist

Requirements: Applicants for the Master of Science degree program must have an undergraduate degree in the biological sciences or a related field. Although there is no minimum GPA for admission into the Master of Science program, successful applicants generally have an undergraduate GPA of 3.000 on a 4.000 point scale. Students with a GPA between 2.500 and 2.999 may be considered for conditional admission. Undergraduate preparation should include a minimum of one year of general chemistry, one year of organic chemistry and one year of physics. Additionally, students are expected to have a minimum of two years of biology courses beyond general biology, including genetics. All applicants are expected to have a minimum of one semester of calculus or statistics. Required Documents: Statement of purpose, and three letters of recommendation. The university requires all non-native English speakers to provide proof of English language proficiency (unless exempt). For more information on test scores and exemptions, please see the University Policy Regarding English Language Proficiency for Admission.
Program name: Master of Science in Biological Sciences - Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics

Requirements:
Admission to the doctoral program is competitive. Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Graduate Studies. A bachelor’s degree in biological sciences or related field with a minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA. Students applying to the doctoral program are strongly encouraged to contact faculty in the department whose research interests match their own. Prior to applying, applicants must identify a faculty member who has agreed to serve as their advisor.
Application Deadlines: Fall: Dec. 1
Additional Admission Requirements:
Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
Curriculum vitae or resume.
Statement of purpose outlining the applicant's research interests and career goals.
Three letters of recommendation submitted directly from the reference.
GRE scores are recommended but not required.
For applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 525 PBT (71 IBT), a minimum IELTS score of 6.0 overall, a minimum PTE score of 48, or a minimum Duolingo English Test score of 105.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biological Sciences - Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics

Requirements:
Applicants for the M.S. degree in Biological Sciences (Ecology and Evolutionary Biology concentration) must meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Arts and Sciences. Additionally, applicants are required to have:
*   An undergraduate GPA of 3.000 or higher on a 4.000 point scale.
*   Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test scores are not required.
*   Three letters of recommendation.
*   A statement of purpose.
*   A curriculum vitae (CV).
Program name: Master of Science in Biological Sciences - Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

Requirements: Master's degree from an accredited institution (e.g., in Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, Fisheries, Forestry, Wildlife, Zoology) for direct admission to the Ph.D. program. In some circumstances, students may be admitted to the Ph.D. program with a bachelor's degree; these cases are reviewed on an individual basis and generally require a minimum 3.000 GPA overall and in the major. Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA. Official transcript(s). Goal Statement/Statement of Purpose (Required). Curriculum Vitae / Resume (Required). Three letters of recommendation (Required). GRE General Test is not required, but applicants may submit scores if they wish. For applicants for whom English is not their first language, an English proficiency exam score is required. The university minimums for these exams are: TOEFL (minimum 79 IBT), IELTS (minimum 6.0 overall band score), PTE (minimum 58), or Duolingo (minimum 105). Applicants must have a faculty sponsor in the Department of Biological Sciences. It is strongly recommended that applicants contact faculty members with whom they wish to work prior to applying to ensure that the faculty member is accepting new students for the intended start term.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biological Sciences - Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Science program in Biological Sciences is highly competitive. To be considered for admission, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in Biology or a related field from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit the following materials:
A completed application
Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities.
A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.000 on a 4.000 point scale is preferred.
General GRE scores are required, with competitive scores on both verbal and quantitative sections. The GRE subject test in Biology is optional.
Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or research abilities.
A statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s research interests, career goals and reasons for pursuing graduate study in Biological Sciences at Kent State University.
A curriculum vitae or resume detailing educational background, research experience, publications, presentations, and any relevant work experience.
Program name: Master of Science in Biological Sciences - Integrative Physiology and Neurobiology

Requirements: Admission to the M.A. degree program requires a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. The undergraduate major should be biology or a related field (e.g., biochemistry, biotechnology or zoology). Undergraduate deficiencies will be assessed by the graduate advisor upon review of the student's undergraduate transcript and may require remedial coursework. The GRE general test scores are not required for admission. The deadline for fall admission is July 1 and for spring admission is November 1.
Program name: Master of Arts in Biology

Requirements: Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale. Official transcripts. Three letters of recommendation. Statement of purpose. Resume or CV. GRE General Test scores are encouraged but not required. International applicants must also meet the university’s English language proficiency requirements. All applicants must apply through the online application portal.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Cellular and Molecular Biology

Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in a biology-related discipline from an accredited college or university. Official transcripts. Minimum cumulative 3.000 undergraduate GPA. Three letters of recommendation. For international students, official TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Sciences - Cellular and Molecular Biology

Requirements: Admission to the doctoral program in Biomedical Sciences is based on a holistic review of all application materials. Requirements include: online application, application fee, official transcripts, a statement of purpose, three letters of recommendation, and official GRE scores (general test) for applicants who do not have a master's degree in a relevant area, or have a master's degree in a relevant area with a GPA below 3.5 on a 4.0 scale. International applicants must submit official TOEFL or IELTS scores. The application requires applicants to list their research, publications and other relevant experience; therefore, a CV is highly recommended.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Sciences - Human Evolutionary Biology

Requirements: Admission to the M.S. in Biomedical Sciences with a concentration in Neuroscience requires an undergraduate degree in a science-related discipline with a minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA. Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Arts and Sciences. In addition, applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, A statement of purpose, A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV), Official GRE scores
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Neurosciences

Requirements: Admission to the Ph.D. in Biomedical Sciences program with a concentration in Neurosciences requires the following: A minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale for baccalaureate coursework and a minimum 3.000 GPA for graduate coursework. Official transcripts. Statement of purpose that describes the applicant’s academic and research experience, research interests and reasons for applying to the Neurosciences program. Curriculum vitae (CV). Three letters of recommendation. International applicants must provide proof of English language proficiency (unless exempt). The GRE general test is not required. Admission decisions are based on a holistic review of all application materials.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Biomedical Sciences - Neurosciences

Requirements: Applicants for admission to the master's program must have a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. All applicants are required to take the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). Official transcripts. Three letters of recommendation. International applicants must provide evidence of English language proficiency.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Pharmacology

Requirements:
Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Graduate Studies, as published in the Graduate Catalog.
A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA.
Minimum 3.000 GPA in biomedical sciences courses.
Official transcripts.
Three letters of recommendation.
A curriculum vitae.
A statement of purpose regarding academic and career goals.
Official GRE general test scores.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences - Physiology Interdisciplinary

Requirements: Admission to the M.S. degree in Chemistry requires a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in chemistry or an allied field, with an undergraduate minimum 2.750 overall GPA on a 4.000 point scale. Applicants are encouraged to submit three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic and/or research abilities. A statement of purpose is required, briefly outlining the applicant's research interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing graduate study in chemistry. Official transcripts from all universities attended. Current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or resume. All applicants are required to take the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) General Test. While there is no minimum GRE score required for admission, applicants are encouraged to score at or above the 50th percentile in the Quantitative and Verbal sections of the GRE. The Analytical Writing section of the GRE is not required. GRE scores should be sent directly to Kent State University (Code 1367). An interview (in person or via video conference) may be required. For international students, proof of English Language Proficiency (e.g., TOEFL, IELTS) is also required.
Program name: Master of Science in Chemistry
Master of Arts in Chemistry

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Science degree in Computer Science is granted to students who hold a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and satisfy the following requirements:
Undergraduate major in computer science or a related discipline. Applicants with an undergraduate major in an unrelated discipline must complete prerequisite undergraduate coursework.
Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000 point scale (for unconditional admission).
Submission of official GRE scores is highly recommended. Students with GRE General Test scores of at least 300 (verbal + quantitative) and a 3.0 analytical writing score are eligible for admission consideration without additional evaluation of academic preparedness.
Three letters of recommendation are required.
A statement of purpose is required.
A resume or curriculum vitae is required.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Arts in Computer Science program requires a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must meet the requirements of the Graduate College and submit additional program materials.
*   Official Transcripts: Transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework must be submitted.
*   GPA: Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and 3.000 in computer science courses.
*   GRE: Applicants are not required to submit GRE scores for admission.
*   Letters of Recommendation: Two letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities.
*   Statement of Purpose: A statement of purpose outlining the applicant’s academic and career goals and how the M.A. program will help achieve them.
*   Resume/Curriculum Vitae: A current resume or curriculum vitae.
*   International Applicants: Additional requirements for international applicants.
Conditional Admission: Applicants who do not meet all criteria may be considered for conditional admission on a case-by-case basis.
Program name: Master of Arts in Computer Science

Requirements:
All applicants must meet the university admission requirements as well as the following program admission requirements:
*   Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution
*   Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall
*   Official transcript(s)
*   Goal statement: Submit a goal statement (2-3 pages, double-spaced) outlining the applicant’s interest in the MA program in Criminology and Criminal Justice, career aspirations and research interests.
*   Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional work
*   Resume/curriculum vitae (CV)
*   Official GRE scores
Program name: Master of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice

Requirements: Applicants must have a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. Students are not required to submit GRE scores. All applicants must submit a writing sample (10–20 pages in length) of their critical prose, ideally on a literary topic. The writing sample should be suitable for use as a diagnostic tool by faculty evaluating the application. All applicants must submit a personal statement (1–2 pages) indicating their interest in graduate study in English at Kent State University and describing their qualifications for success in the program. Applicants for the M.A. in English (Concentration for Teachers) are also encouraged to submit a current curriculum vitae or resume.
Program name: Master of Arts in English (Concentration for Teachers)

Requirements:
Applicants to the M.A. in English program (both literature and writing tracks) must hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants are typically expected to have an undergraduate major in English or in a closely related field. Successful applicants normally have a minimum 3.0 GPA in undergraduate work. While the GRE is not required, applications from students with strong GRE scores are welcome.
Applicants must submit the following materials to the Department of English in addition to the online application:
A Statement of Purpose: Please include a 1-2 page essay describing your academic and professional goals and how the M.A. program in English (Literature and Writing) at Kent State University will help you meet those goals.
A Writing Sample: Please submit a critical essay or an analytical paper of approximately 10-20 pages that demonstrates your ability to analyze literary texts or produce academic prose in a similar field. If you are applying to the Writing Track and have substantial creative writing experience, you may submit a sample of your creative work in lieu of a critical essay (20-25 pages of prose or 8-10 poems).
Three Letters of Recommendation: Letters should be from faculty members or others who can attest to your academic and intellectual abilities.
Transcripts: Upload unofficial transcripts with your online application. Official transcripts are required upon admission.
Program name: Master of Arts in English (Literature and Writing)

Requirements: Applicants for the M.A. in Teaching English as a Second Language program are admitted conditionally or fully, depending on their qualifications and the availability of space in the program. Requirements for admission include: A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. A minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA overall and in the major for full admission. An undergraduate major in English, linguistics, modern and classical language studies, communication, education or a related area (e.g., journalism, philosophy, speech pathology, anthropology, sociology). Minimum 6 semester hours in English grammar. Minimum 6 semester hours in a foreign language (preferably 12 semester hours). Two letters of recommendation from persons familiar with the applicant's academic work and potential for graduate study. A sample of academic writing in English, approximately 5-10 pages long. A brief statement of purpose (1-2 pages) indicating the applicant's academic interests and professional goals related to TESL. Official transcript(s). International applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency through one of the following methods: TOEFL score (minimum 79 iBT, 550 PBT), IELTS score (minimum 6.5), PTE Academic score (minimum 58), Duolingo English Test score (minimum 105), or successful completion of Kent State University's ESL program.
Program name: Master of Arts in Teaching English as a Second Language
Master of Science in Geography

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Arts in History program requires an undergraduate major in history or at least 24 semester hours of credit in history. Students whose undergraduate major is not history, but who meet the 24-hour credit requirement may be admitted only with the permission of the graduate coordinator. In addition, students must meet the following minimum requirements:
*   Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA overall or in the last two years of undergraduate study.
*   Official transcript(s)
*   A statement of purpose: explaining the applicant’s academic interests and preparation for graduate study in history.
*   A writing sample: a historical paper of 5-10 pages (no longer than 20 pages) that demonstrates the applicant’s research and analytical abilities.
*   Three letters of recommendation.
*   A curriculum vitae or résumé.
*   International students must meet Kent State University’s English language proficiency requirement.
Program name: Master of Arts in History

Requirements: To apply to the Master of Liberal Studies program, please submit the following materials through the university's online application system: Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. A statement of purpose outlining academic goals and interests. A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV). A writing sample (e.g., a term paper, essay, or research project from a previous course) that demonstrates the applicant's ability to engage in graduate-level scholarly writing. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic abilities and potential for graduate study. Applicants must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale for undergraduate coursework. International applicants must also meet Kent State University's English language proficiency requirements.
Program name: Master of Liberal Studies (L.S.M.)

Requirements: Applicants for admission to the Master of Arts in Mathematics for Secondary Teachers program must have an undergraduate degree in mathematics, mathematics education or a related field; a minimum 2.750 overall undergraduate GPA; a minimum 3.000 GPA in mathematics courses; and two letters of recommendation. Applicants whose undergraduate major is not mathematics or mathematics education may be required to complete undergraduate mathematics courses before being accepted into the program.
Program name: Master of Arts in Mathematics for Secondary Teachers

Requirements: Application deadlines for admission to the Master of Arts (M.A.) or Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Mathematics are July 1 for fall, November 1 for spring and March 1 for summer. In addition to the general university admission requirements, applicants for admission to the M.A. or Ph.D. program in Mathematics must meet the following requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and 3.000 in Mathematics courses. A minimum of 24 credit hours of undergraduate mathematics courses at the 30000 level or higher, including a year of advanced calculus/real analysis (MATH 40011/40012) and a semester of abstract algebra (MATH 41001). The GRE General Test is required. Three letters of recommendation are required. A statement of purpose is required. International students must provide evidence of English language proficiency (unless from a country where English is the official language or from an institution where the language of instruction is English).
Program name: Master of Arts in Pure Mathematics

Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree in mathematics or a closely related field, a minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA, an undergraduate record demonstrating sufficient preparation for graduate work in mathematics (e.g., strong performance in advanced undergraduate mathematics courses such as real analysis, complex analysis and abstract algebra). Applicants are required to submit the following: Official transcripts, Three letters of recommendation, A statement of purpose, A curriculum vitae. TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test Scores are required for international applicants whose native language is not English. For details, please refer to the Kent State University Office of Global Education.
Program name: Master of Science in Pure Mathematics

Requirements: Applicants for admission to the Master of Arts in French must have an undergraduate major in French or its equivalent, as determined by the graduate coordinator. Applicants are expected to have a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and a 3.000 GPA in French. International applicants must meet university admission requirements and hold a bachelor's degree comparable to a U.S. bachelor's degree.
Program name: Master of Arts in French

Requirements:
Applicants must meet the requirements of the Graduate College as well as the following program-specific requirements:
*   Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA.
*   Baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution.
*   Two letters of recommendation.
*   One official transcript from each college or university attended.
*   A statement of purpose of 300-500 words, indicating academic background in Classics/Latin and outlining intellectual interests and goals.
*   One writing sample of 10-15 pages (approximately 3,000-4,000 words), preferably a revised term paper on a classical topic or related subject. The sample should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to conduct research and write an argumentative essay.
*   The GRE (Graduate Record Examination) General Test is optional.
*   International applicants must meet English language proficiency requirements as published in the Graduate Catalog.
Program name: Master of Arts in Latin

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the Kent State University Graduate School, as well as the following specific requirements: Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in Spanish or a related field (e.g., world languages, comparative literature) with a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and 3.000 GPA in Spanish or related coursework. Statement of purpose. Writing sample of 5-10 pages (in Spanish or English). Three letters of recommendation. Official transcript(s). For applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), 213 (computer-based) or 550 (paper-based), or an equivalent score on an appropriate English language proficiency test (e.g., IELTS, PTE). This requirement is waived for applicants who have earned an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited college or university in the United States or other English-speaking country.
Program name: Master of Arts in Spanish

Requirements: Admission to the M.A. in Translation program is competitive. Successful applicants generally have an undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or higher. For full admission consideration, applicants should submit the following documents: Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA; Official transcript(s); Curriculum Vitae or Resume; Statement of purpose; Two letters of recommendation; Writing sample; English language proficiency (for international applicants).
Program name: Master of Arts in Translation

Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Science in Physics program is competitive. Applicants are expected to have a bachelor's degree in physics or a related field from an accredited college or university. All applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the College of Arts and Sciences Graduate Studies and the following minimum requirements for admission to the Master of Science in Physics program:
*   Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA
*   Official transcript(s)
*   Three letters of recommendation
Additional admission materials include the following:
*   Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume
*   Statement of Purpose
*   Official GRE general test scores
For applicants whose native language is not English, a minimum score of 79 on the TOEFL iBT (with a minimum of 20 in each section), or a minimum of 6.5 on the IELTS (with a minimum of 6.0 in each section) is required. The TOEFL/IELTS requirement is waived for students who have earned a degree from a college or university in the United States or another English-speaking country.
Program name: Master of Science in Physics

Requirements: The general university admission requirements are discussed in the Admissions section of this Catalog. In addition, the Master of Arts degree in Physics requires: Official transcript(s), Undergraduate GPA of 2.750 for all undergraduate work (3.000 for all undergraduate work in the major), Three letters of recommendation, Personal statement, GRE general test scores (analytical writing section is not required), For international students, a minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), MELAB score of 74, IELTS score of 6.5 or PTE score of 53.
Program name: Master of Arts in Physics

Requirements:
All applicants must meet the university admission requirements as well as the following program requirements:
*   A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall.
*   Submit official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
*   Submit a curriculum vitae or resume.
*   Submit a goal statement (statement of purpose) outlining the applicant’s academic and professional goals, including their reasons for seeking graduate study in political science at Kent State University and their particular areas of interest.
*   Submit three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable about the applicant’s academic record and qualifications for graduate study.
*   Official GRE scores are not required for admission to the M.A. program.
*   International applicants must meet university requirements for admission. Minimum English language proficiency test score requirements for admission for the M.A. program: minimum 79 TOEFL iBT (with no section below 17), 6.5 IELTS (with no section below 5.5), 58 PTE Academic or 110 Duolingo.
Program name: Master of Arts in Political Science

Requirements: Applicants to the Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.) program must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university and a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. Applicants must apply for admission through the Kent State University online application. In addition, applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Statement of purpose (describing professional goals and interest in the M.P.A. degree). Professional resume or curriculum vitae. Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities. For applicants whose first language is not English, an official TOEFL or IELTS score. Applicants may apply for a waiver of the GRE general test by documenting one of the following: An undergraduate GPA of 3.000 or higher. A master's or doctoral degree from an accredited institution. Evidence of significant professional experience or professional certification. (To be evaluated by the MPA director).
Program name: Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.)

Requirements: Students apply through the Kent State University School of Graduate Studies. The requirements are a strong undergraduate record (including some courses in philosophy), three letters of recommendation, a writing sample, a statement of purpose, and a CV. We do not require the GRE. International students must also submit TOEFL/IELTS scores.
Program name: Master of Arts in Philosophy
Master of Arts in Clinical Psychology

Requirements: Applicants must meet the general requirements of the Kent State University Graduate School, as well as the following specific program requirements: Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA overall and in psychology coursework. Official transcripts Three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant’s academic performance. Goal statement outlining academic and professional goals, research interests, and why the applicant is interested in our MA program. Official GRE general test scores. International applicants must also meet the English language proficiency requirements as defined in the Kent State University Graduate Catalog.
Program name: Master of Arts in Psychological Sciences

Requirements: Admission to the Master of Arts in Sociology program requires an undergraduate degree from an accredited college or university. A 3.00 GPA on a 4.00 scale in undergraduate work is usually expected. Students whose undergraduate GPA is less than 3.00 may be admitted conditionally based on other evidence of academic potential, such as a strong statement of purpose, academic letters of recommendation or a professional resume. Students from disciplines other than sociology are welcome to apply. Applicants whose undergraduate major is not in sociology, or a related social science, may be required to take additional undergraduate coursework prior to or concurrently with graduate courses. All applicants are required to submit the following: Official transcripts, A statement of purpose, Three academic letters of recommendation, A professional resume or curriculum vitae.
Program name: Master of Arts in Sociology

Requirements: Minimum 3.000 GPA in undergraduate major coursework (or related fields) and/or graduate coursework. Admission to the Educational Technology program is competitive. Applicants must meet the requirements of the College of Education, Health and Human Services (EHHS) and the Educational Technology program. Applicants must submit: Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework completed to date. Three (3) letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's academic and/or professional abilities. A personal statement that describes the applicant's academic and professional background, reasons for pursuing a master's degree in educational technology, and career goals. Applicants should highlight their experiences with and interest in technology, teaching and learning, and educational environments. A current professional resume or curriculum vitae (CV) that outlines the applicant's work experience, educational background, professional development activities, publications, presentations, and any other relevant accomplishments. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required for admission to the Master of Education in Educational Technology program.
Program name: Master of Education in Educational Technology

Requirements: Applicants for the Master of Science in Exercise Physiology program must meet the following requirements: Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university; Minimum 2.750 cumulative GPA; Official transcripts; Three letters of recommendation; Goal statement; CV/resume; GRE general test results (optional for applicants with an undergraduate GPA of 3.000 or higher); Minimum TOEFL score of 79 (internet-based), 213 (computer-based) or 550 (paper-based) for international applicants; Minimum IELTS score of 6.0 for international applicants; Minimum PTE Academic score of 58 for international applicants.
Program name: Master of Science in Exercise Physiology

Requirements: All applicants must meet the university admission requirements as well as the following program requirements: Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA; Minimum 3.000 graduate GPA; Master’s degree in Exercise Physiology or related field from an accredited institution; Official transcripts; Three letters of recommendation; Goal statement; Curriculum Vitae (CV); Official GRE scores. Applicants must also complete an interview with exercise physiology faculty members.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Exercise Physiology

Requirements: To be considered for admission into the Ph.D. in Higher Education Administration program, applicants must hold a master’s degree in Higher Education Administration or a related field (e.g., student personnel, educational administration, business, counseling) from an accredited institution. A minimum 3.000 cumulative master's degree GPA is required for admission. All applicants must complete the online application, which requires submission of the following materials: Application for Graduate Admission, Official Transcripts, Three Letters of Recommendation, Resume/Curriculum Vitae, Statement of Purpose, Official GRE Scores, Writing Sample, Interview.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Higher Education Administration

Requirements: To apply for the Ed.S. degree in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs, you must meet the following requirements and complete the online application process. A completed application to the College of Graduate Studies, which includes a personal goal statement, a current resume/curriculum vitae (CV), three letters of recommendation and official transcripts. Master's degree from an accredited institution. Official transcripts must be sent to the College of Graduate Studies. An undergraduate GPA of 3.00 on a 4.00 scale and a graduate GPA of 3.50 on a 4.00 scale for unconditional admission.
Program name: Education Specialist in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs

Requirements: To be considered for admission into the Master of Education in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs (HEASA) program, applicants must have: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000 point scale. Official transcripts. Goals statement addressing why the applicant is interested in the program, the applicant's career goals, and an explanation of any experience the applicant has had working in higher education or with college students. Resume or vita. Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's academic and/or professional potential. Diversity statement or response to diversity prompt. A brief (1-3 page) writing sample is required, but it does not need to be a formal research paper (e.g., a paper from an undergraduate class or a professional memorandum).
Program name: Master of Education in Higher Education Administration and Student Affairs

Requirements:
To be considered for admission into the online Doctor of Education in Interprofessional Leadership (Ed.D.) program, you must meet the following requirements:
*   A master’s degree from an accredited institution.
*   A minimum 3.00 GPA on a 4.00 scale for graduate coursework.
*   Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended.
*   A professional resume or curriculum vitae (CV).
*   A statement of purpose outlining your professional experience, reasons for pursuing this degree, and career aspirations.
*   Three letters of recommendation addressing your academic and professional leadership skills.
*   An interview with program faculty.
*   The GRE is NOT required for admission to this program.
Program name: Doctor of Education in Interprofessional Leadership

Requirements: Admission to the Master of Arts in Learning Science program is competitive. Applicants must demonstrate academic preparedness and a strong commitment to learning sciences. In addition to the university's general graduate admission requirements, applicants must meet the following program-specific requirements: Baccalaureate Degree: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. GPA: A minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA on a 4.000 point scale for undergraduate coursework. Applicants with a GPA below 3.000 but above 2.750 may be considered for conditional admission. Statement of Purpose: A well-written statement of purpose (approximately 500-750 words) outlining the applicant's academic and professional background, research interests, career goals, and reasons for pursuing the M.A. in Learning Science. The statement should also describe how the program aligns with their aspirations. Letters of Recommendation: Two letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant's academic abilities, research potential, and suitability for graduate study. At least one letter should be from a faculty member. Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV): A current resume or CV detailing educational background, work experience, research activities, publications, presentations, awards, and any other relevant accomplishments. Transcripts: Official transcripts from all previously attended institutions. English Language Proficiency: International applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency through one of the following: TOEFL, IELTS, PTE Academic, or Duolingo English Test scores.
Program name: Master of Arts in Learning Science

Requirements: Master’s degree in a related field from an accredited institution. Consideration will be given to those with a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution, who demonstrate extraordinary promise. Minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale (for both master's and bachelor's degrees if applicable). Evidence of a commitment to research: For example, master’s thesis, research course projects, scholarly presentations, or publications. If no prior research experience, applicants may substitute a research proposal to demonstrate understanding of research processes (e.g., a statement of a problem, review of literature, methodology, expected outcomes, and discussion of implications relevant to learning science). A personal statement that outlines academic and professional experiences and clearly defines research interests. An up-to-date Curriculum Vitae (CV) or resume that details professional experiences, academic background, skills, and accomplishments. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant’s academic and/or professional capabilities and potential for success in a doctoral program. Official transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. For applicants with an international degree, a TOEFL score (or equivalent, e.g., IELTS) with a minimum score of 79 (internet-based) or 550 (paper-based), unless they have completed a previous degree from an accredited institution in the U.S. GRE scores are NOT required. Successful completion of an interview (by invitation only) with the Learning Science Program Faculty.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Learning Science

Requirements: Admission to the Master of Science in Nutrition requires a minimum cumulative 2.75 undergraduate GPA and a bachelor's degree in nutrition, dietetics or a related area (e.g., biology, biochemistry, food science, public health, exercise science) from an accredited institution. Students with degrees in unrelated areas are still eligible for admission consideration, but may be required to complete specific undergraduate coursework with a grade of "B" or better prior to or concurrent with graduate study. These courses typically include: CHEM 10050 Fundamentals of Chemistry or higher, CHEM 10051 Fundamentals of Chemistry Lab or higher, BIOL 10101 Introduction to Biological Sciences or higher, BIOL 10102 Introduction to Biological Sciences Lab or higher, NUTR 20810 Science of Food or equivalent, NUTR 30820 Macronutrients and Metabolism or equivalent, NUTR 30821 Micronutrients and Metabolism or equivalent, NUTR 30830 Nutrition Throughout the Life Cycle or equivalent, NUTR 40830 Medical Nutrition Therapy or equivalent, NUTR 40831 Medical Nutrition Therapy Lab or equivalent, NUTR 40840 Community Nutrition or equivalent. Meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee admission. All application materials are reviewed and evaluated holistically. The applicant must apply through the Kent State University Admissions portal.
Program name: Master of Science in Nutrition

Requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA (on a 4.000 point scale) for unconditional admission. A copy of your official license/certificate from the Ohio Department of Education. If you do not have an Ohio teaching license, you must provide a copy of your teaching license from your state of residence. If you do not have a valid teaching license, you may be conditionally admitted to the program. Official transcripts for all colleges and universities attended. A goal statement (250-500 words) describing your academic and career goals and how the M.Ed. in Reading Specialization program aligns with these goals. A current vita/resume. Two letters of recommendation. International students must meet the university’s English language proficiency requirement.
Program name: Master of Education in Reading Specialization
Master of Education in Research, Measurement, and Statistics

Requirements:
Master's degree from an accredited institution. A master's degree in a quantitative social science, such as educational psychology, psychology, sociology, public health, statistics, applied statistics, biostatistics, psychometrics, measurement or related field is preferred.
Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale.
Minimum 3.500 graduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale.
Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended.
Goal statement (500-1,000 words) that describes:
Your educational and professional experiences and future career goals.
Your reasons for pursuing the Ph.D. in Research, Measurement and Statistics.
Your research interests and how they align with the program's faculty expertise.
Curriculum vitae or resume.
Three letters of recommendation addressing the applicant’s academic and professional experiences and capabilities.
GRE General Test scores (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing). Applicants may be granted a waiver from the GRE requirement based on a strong academic record (GPA of 3.500 or higher in a relevant master's degree program) or significant relevant professional experience. Applicants seeking a waiver should indicate their request and justification in their goal statement. The program coordinator will review waiver requests.
Interview with faculty via phone or video conference.
International students must meet the university's English language proficiency requirement.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Research, Measurement, and Statistics

Requirements:
Requirements for admission include:
1. Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale for baccalaureate degree.
2. A complete online application (including official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, non-refundable application fee and other application materials specified).
3. Statement of purpose: Submit a 500-750 word essay addressing: (a) relevant experience, (b) career goals, (c) self-awareness regarding academic strengths, areas for growth, and diversity awareness, and (d) reasons for applying to this program at Kent State University.
4. Official scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test. There are no minimum GRE scores required for admission.
5. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who are able to speak to the applicant’s academic and professional potential for success in a graduate program.
6. A current professional resume or curriculum vitae (CV) that includes educational background, professional work experience, volunteer work and relevant skills.
7. Complete a video interview conducted online following submission of the online application.
8. Completion of an undergraduate course in statistics. Students who have not completed an undergraduate statistics course will be required to take EPSY 22294 Statistical Reasoning in Psychology or an approved equivalent course during their first year of the program.
Program name: Master of Education in School Counseling

Requirements: Applicants to the Master of Education degree program in School Psychology must meet the following requirements: Minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA. Submission of the online application. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. A current resume or curriculum vitae. Three letters of recommendation submitted through the online application system. An essay describing your professional goals, previous experience, and interest in school psychology at Kent State University. Official GRE General Test scores (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) may be submitted and will be considered, but are not required for admission.
Program name: Master of Education in School Psychology

Requirements: Online Application for Graduate Admission: Students must complete the online application for graduate admission for the School Psychology Ed.S. program and submit the $45 non-refundable application fee. Transcripts: An official transcript of all college-level work (undergraduate and graduate) must be submitted directly to the Office of Graduate Admissions. GPA: Minimum 3.000 cumulative undergraduate GPA. International Applicants: Additional requirements for international applicants include TOEFL/IELTS scores, a Declaration of Finances statement and evaluation of international transcripts.
Program name: Education Specialist in School Psychology

Requirements: Completed online graduate application. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA. Minimum 3.500 graduate GPA (if applicable). Three letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of the applicant’s academic and professional abilities. At least one recommendation should be from a professor who taught the applicant in a psychology course. Resume or curriculum vitae. Personal statement addressing the applicant’s professional goals, academic and research interests, and experiences relevant to school psychology. The personal statement should also indicate how the Kent State School Psychology program can help the applicant achieve their goals. Official GRE scores (verbal, quantitative and analytical writing) taken within five years of the application date. The GRE requirement is waived for applicants who have earned a master's degree in School Psychology. Interview with program faculty. Interviews are by invitation only after review of application materials. TOEFL, IELTS, PTE, Duolingo English Test or MELAB scores for international applicants whose native language is not English. A master's degree in school psychology (preferred, but not required). Completion of undergraduate course work in the following areas: developmental psychology, abnormal psychology, statistics, research methods, and introduction to psychology.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in School Psychology

Requirements: Applicants to the M.A.T. Secondary Education program must meet the general admission requirements of the College of Education, Health and Human Services and the following program requirements: Minimum 2.750 undergraduate cumulative GPA. Completion of undergraduate major or equivalent coursework from an accredited institution in an area that leads to a teaching license in Ohio. Verification of a clear background check. Satisfactory performance on the entrance essay. Two letters of recommendation. Submit an application with all required materials. Official transcripts from all universities and colleges attended. Interview with a faculty member may be required. Statement of purpose outlining why the applicant wishes to teach, the grade levels and subjects they wish to teach and their related experiences.
Program name: Master of Arts in Teaching Secondary Education

Requirements: Admission requirements are in addition to the university graduate admission requirements. Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution, a minimum 2.750 undergraduate GPA, and submit official transcripts, one letter of recommendation (from an academic or professional reference who can speak to the applicant's potential for success in graduate studies), a goal statement (500-750 words) that addresses the applicant's reason for pursuing the M.Ed. in Special Education, professional and/or research interests and professional goals, and a current resume or curriculum vitae.
Program name: Master of Education in Special Education

Requirements: Application to the Office of Graduate Admissions (online application, application fee, transcripts, etc.). Master's degree in Special Education or a related field. If related field, candidate must provide evidence of coursework/experience in special education commensurate with initial teaching licensure requirements. Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale. Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended. English language proficiency (international students only). Statement of purpose: a two-page maximum essay describing your career goals, how the Ed.S. program will help you achieve those goals and what you feel you will contribute to the program. Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can speak to the applicant’s academic and/or professional abilities. Current resume or vita. GRE scores are optional. TOEFL/IELTS scores for applicants for whom English is not their native language.
Program name: Education Specialist in Special Education

Requirements: Official transcript(s). Master’s degree in special education or a related field (e.g., educational psychology, early childhood education, educational studies, curriculum and instruction, speech-language pathology, social work) with a minimum 3.000 GPA. Two letters of recommendation. Resume or curriculum vitae. Goal statement that addresses the applicant’s academic and professional experiences, reasons for pursuing a Ph.D. in Special Education at Kent State University and future goals related to the field of special education. Academic writing sample (e.g., master’s thesis, research paper, publication). GRE general test scores. Interview with Special Education faculty. For international applicants, a minimum 79 TOEFL iBT score or equivalent is required. For more information on institutional requirements for English language proficiency, visit the international admission page.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy in Special Education
Master of Education in Educational Psychology

Requirements:
Applicants for the Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) degree in Interprofessional Leadership must have completed a master's degree from an accredited institution and submit the following to the Office of Graduate Admissions:
*   Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate coursework
*   Two letters of recommendation from individuals knowledgeable of the applicant's academic and professional abilities.
*   Statement of purpose addressing the applicant's educational and professional goals and how the Ed.D. program aligns with those goals.
*   Curriculum Vitae (CV) or professional resume highlighting educational background, professional experience, research activities, publications, presentations, and any other relevant accomplishments.
*   Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required for admission to this program.
Program name: Doctor of Education (Ed.D.)

Requirements:
Admission to the D.N.P. program is based on a careful review of academic record, professional experience, goals and recommendations. In addition to the general graduate admission requirements, applicants must meet the following program requirements:
- Master's degree with a major in nursing from an accredited college or university.
- Minimum 3.000 undergraduate GPA on a 4.000-point scale.
- Current, unencumbered registered nurse (RN) license in Ohio or the state in which clinical experiences will be completed.
- Completion of a statistics course with a minimum C grade within five years prior to admission. An applicant who has not completed a statistics course or does not meet the five-year requirement must take a statistics course prior to or concurrently with the first clinical course.
- Graduate-level advanced pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology and advanced health assessment courses from an accredited college or university. Students who have not completed these courses prior to admission may take them at Kent State University prior to or concurrently with the first D.N.P. clinical course.
- Statement of Purpose that describes why the applicant is seeking a D.N.P. degree, career goals and experience in leadership, evidence-based practice and quality improvement.
- Curriculum Vitae or Resume.
- Three letters of recommendation from individuals who can address the applicant's academic and leadership abilities.
- Interview with a faculty member, if requested.
- English language proficiency requirements for international students.
Program name: Doctor of Nursing Practice (D.N.P.)

Requirements:
To be considered for admission to the College of Podiatric Medicine, applicants must meet the following minimum requirements:
